clue.text: Taken me shopping, partly as trap

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone recalls being taken shopping and feeling ensnared by it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnare or entangle something in a net is to catch it, which is what a trap does.

clue.text: Forecast that old flame is getting kissed, say

indicators.note: say tells the solver the phrase before it is to be spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: an old flame is an EX, and kissed is PECKED; together they are spoken as one word

explanation.surface: Predicting that a former partner is about to get a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: EX plus PECKED, said quickly, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To forecast something is to anticipate or predict that it will happen.

clue.text: Disperse thin gloom of nightly illumination

indicators.note: disperse means scatter, so the letters of the following words are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to break up a faint darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disperse' rearranges the nine letters of THIN GLOOM.
explanation.definitionFit: The light from the moon is the glow that brightens the sky after dark.

clue.text: Carbonated soft drink in espresso daiquiri

indicators.note: in says the drink sits inside the letters of the two words after it

explanation.surface: Asking whether a fizzy mixer goes into a coffee cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to espresSO DAiquiri.
explanation.definitionFit: A fizzy water or pop is a bubbly non-alcoholic beverage.

parts.note: an ass is a foolish person
first is written 1ST, with the figure one read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A clumsy person is given first aid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first aid' looks like one phrase, but 'first' gives IST (1ST) and 'aid' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To aid someone is to help them.

definitions.meaning: a ... person is frank and truthful
the home ... is the final stretch of a racecourse

explanation.definitionFit: Straightforward dealing is honest; the final flat stretch of a racetrack is the finishing run.

indicators.note: in says the word lies inside the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Tempers flare among the singers in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to choIR Eventually; 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is a literary word for wrath or fury.

definitions.meaning: read as one who sums: someone who totes, or adds up, a total
to reel is to stagger unsteadily

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who adds figures up totes them; staggering about is walking unsteadily.

clue.text: In favour of support for the most part

indicators.note: for the most part means take most of the word, dropping its final letter

parts.note: a prop is something that supports

explanation.surface: Backing a cause by giving it mostly support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' drops the last letter of PROP.
explanation.definitionFit: Being for something, as in pros and cons, means arguing on its side.

clue.text: Man put off by domestic cleaner

parts.note: to deter someone is to put them off
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A man is discouraged by his cleaning lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'domestic cleaner' looks like a person, but it is a washing product; 'by' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Washing powder or liquid is a household product for cleaning clothes and dishes.

clue.text: Model singer entertaining monarch given reprimand

parts.note: the Model T was an early Ford car, so model gives T

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A model and a singer play host to royalty and get told off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' is the Model T Ford; 'entertaining' is the container signal, with the monarch as the guest held inside the singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing-down or scolding is a stern lecture given to someone at fault.

indicators.note: behind puts the lieutenant's letters after the firm's

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: An army officer backs a solid horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A young male horse is called by this name.

clue.text: In addition, kept in gold Shakespearean castle

indicators.note: kept means held inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: else means besides, in addition
taken as written
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A treasure-filled fortress from the plays, with gold stored inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept' is the container signal: the two short pieces sit inside the synonym for 'in addition'. OR for gold comes from heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is set at the Danish royal castle of this name in Shakespeare's tragedy.

indicators.note: involves means wraps around, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: ordnance is military guns and artillery
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Big guns are subject to a single rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involves' puts I inside ORDNANCE; the spellings differ by that one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A local by-law or decree is an authoritative rule.

parts.note: a trial is an ordeal or hardship
to run something is to organise it

explanation.surface: Arranging something gruelling as a rehearsal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to organise' looks like an anagram signal; here 'organise' is simply RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal or test drive done before the real thing is a dry run.

indicators.note: rocks means shakes up, so the letters of the words before are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man's garden is decorated with stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' looks like garden stones, but it signals rearranging HIS GARDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish or object decorated with a finishing trim has been adorned.

definitions.meaning: read as ..., to coil once more

explanation.definitionFit: Shrinking back in fright is a sudden jerk away; coiling a rope a second time is a re-winding.

indicators.note: to hold says the two words contain the name within their letters

explanation.surface: A woman named Ethel is allowed to embrace a young lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold' points to etHEL ENAbled.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female first name, as of the mother of Constantine.

indicators.note: suffer here means be damaged, so the letters of the word are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to make a sergeant endure hardship and turn enemies against each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffer' rearranges SERGEANT.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone is to turn them unfriendly or distant.

indicators.note: sort here is a verb meaning arrange, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tidy kind of wager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges NEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker the opening bet each player puts into the pot is called this.

indicators.note: we hear means the clue word's synonym is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a pip is a fruit seed

explanation.surface: We are told a fruit pip gives a crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yield' looks like a harvest beside 'pip', but it means give way.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender territory or give way in an argument is to concede.

indicators.note: making here means forming, so the letters of the two words are made into something new

explanation.surface: A cricketer intentionally resists scoring runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' rearranges OPPOSE and RUN together.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something intentionally rather than by accident.

clue.text: Some expansion in the cooking vessel

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the vessel is found within the next word

explanation.surface: A bit of extra space in the saucepan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' points to exPANsion; 'in the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot used on the stove for frying or boiling.

clue.text: Born into extreme poverty without end

indicators.note: without end means the final letter of the word is removed

parts.note: need is a state of extreme poverty

explanation.surface: Someone born into the depths of hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without end' drops the last letter of NEED; 'into' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Used before a married woman's maiden name, this French word means born with that surname.

definitions.meaning: the inner layer of fabric sewn inside a coat
growing lined, as a face does with age

explanation.definitionFit: A coat's inner fabric layer; a face gaining creases is getting lined.

clue.text: Mrs Peron is after info in Swiss city

indicators.note: is after places the name of Mrs Peron following the word for information

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
Eva Peron was the wife of Argentina's President Juan Peron

explanation.surface: Eva Peron goes looking for information in a Swiss city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is after' looks like 'is seeking', but it is a placement signal; GEN is informal British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: This lakeside city in western Switzerland is home to many international bodies.
